description:
Build AI Agents That Do More Than Answer Questions

A conventional chatbot gives an answer; a properly designed AI agent can also retrieve approved information, choose a permitted tool, evaluate a result and continue toward a goal. The 6 Month Agentic AI Training in Mohali page at techcadd introduces that end-to-end development process. Learners move from Python and APIs to LangChain, RAG, LangGraph and a deployable capstone. The emphasis is on building explainable systems with boundaries, not claiming that autonomous software is always correct.

What Is Agentic AI and How Is It Different from Generative AI?

Generative AI creates text, images or other outputs in response to an input. Agentic AI adds application logic that can plan steps, call tools and react to feedback. For example, a model may summarize a support policy, while an agentic application may retrieve the relevant policy, inspect an allowed ticket record and draft the appropriate next action. These systems still rely on model outputs that can be wrong; permissions, testing and human oversight remain important.

Why Learn Python and APIs Before Building Agents?

Python programming provides a practical foundation for AI application development. Learners work with functions, packages, virtual environments, JSON, HTTP requests, error handling and Git before combining them with language-model APIs. These skills matter when a document loader fails, a tool returns unexpected data or an integration needs debugging. Starting with software fundamentals makes later LLM application development more reliable and allows projects to be tested and maintained.

LangChain for LLM Application Development

LangChain helps developers connect language models, prompts, document processing, retrievers and tools into applications. Training activities can include structured outputs, reusable prompt templates, request validation and safe API integrations. Students learn to treat framework components as building blocks rather than magic shortcuts. A simple, inspectable workflow is often better than a complicated agent when the task follows a fixed sequence.

RAG Training: Connect Language Models with Relevant Knowledge

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) supplies a model with selected information retrieved from an approved knowledge base. A typical workflow extracts text, splits documents into chunks, creates embeddings, indexes them in a vector database and retrieves useful passages for a question. Learners practise source attribution and refusal when evidence is missing. RAG improves access to context but does not guarantee factual correctness, making evaluation an essential part of the course.

Vector Databases, Embeddings and Search Quality

An embedding is a numeric representation used to compare similarity between pieces of information. Tools such as Chroma, FAISS, Qdrant and pgvector support different retrieval configurations. Learners explore chunk sizes, metadata filters, search results and basic retrieval evaluation. The aim is not to memorize every vendor; it is to understand how retrieval choices affect the relevance of information passed to an LLM.

Build AI Agents with Safe Tool Calling

AI agents may call functions, read an approved database or interact with a connected service. This introduces risks that are absent from a simple text response. A suitable training exercise defines tool schemas, limits permissions, logs decisions and handles failed calls. Learners can build a controlled support assistant that drafts recommendations without changing real records automatically. They learn when to use an agent and when a predictable fixed workflow is safer.

LangGraph for Stateful and Human-in-the-Loop Workflows

LangGraph is useful when an application needs branching logic, persistent state or a step that pauses for human input. Learners can model an agent workflow as nodes and transitions, add checkpoints and design approval gates before consequential actions. An example is an agent that prepares an operational request but waits for a person to approve it. This turns the concept of responsible automation into a concrete development pattern.

Multi-Agent Systems and MCP: When Are They Useful?

A multi-agent system separates responsibilities, for example research, drafting and verification, while a shared workflow coordinates the results. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard for making tools and context available to AI applications. Learners explore these concepts through bounded prototypes, including the cost and complexity of additional agents. The course avoids treating multiple agents as automatically better than a single well-designed workflow.

How Do You Evaluate the Reliability of an AI Agent?

A working demo is not sufficient evidence that an agent is ready for a production environment. Tests should cover retrieval quality, unsupported claims, tool permissions, failures, latency and cost. With pytest and tracing tools such as LangSmith, learners can compare outputs against expected behaviors and inspect failed runs. Good evaluation asks whether the system completed the intended task safely and whether a human can audit what happened.

Projects and Portfolio: Show the Code Behind the Demo

During the six-month roadmap, students can create a document knowledge assistant, a support triage agent, a human-approved workflow, a research checker and a final integrated application. Each proposed project has a clear purpose, bounded dataset, measurable checks and a deliverable such as a README, demo or test report. A strong Agentic AI portfolio makes design decisions visible; screenshots without implementation evidence are less useful in technical interviews.

Deployment, GitHub and Career Preparation

FastAPI, Docker and GitHub help turn isolated experiments into understandable application projects. Students can learn how to expose an endpoint, manage environment variables, write automated tests and document deployment steps. These skills connect Agentic AI with broader software engineering roles such as AI application developer and LLM integration trainee. Employability depends on portfolio quality, programming ability, interview performance and hiring requirements, not course completion alone.

Who Can Join Agentic AI Training in Mohali?

This pathway is relevant to B.Tech, BCA, MCA and related students, graduates, software developers, career changers and professionals exploring AI automation. Learners familiar with basic programming may progress faster, while beginners may need extra practice with Python, functions and APIs. syllabus.title: Weeks 1–2 | Python and Developer Foundations

topics: Tokens, context windows and model constraints

syllabus.body: Explore how large language models generate responses, where they fail and how to request schema-constrained outputs that downstream applications can trust.
syllabus.project: A prompt-and-output evaluation notebook with valid JSON extraction.

syllabus.title: Weeks 5–6 | LangChain and Application Patterns
syllabus.body: Connect model calls to reusable application components, keep data boundaries explicit and test each integration before enabling automated actions.

syllabus.body: Learn the complete retrieval-augmented generation workflow: prepare approved content, index it, retrieve relevant passages and answer with traceable citations.

syllabus.title: Weeks 10–12 | Vector Search and RAG Evaluation
topics: Metadata filtering and hybrid search concepts
Faithfulness, retrieval quality and test sets
syllabus.body: Improve a working RAG assistant with controlled experiments. Measure retrieval relevance and answer grounding rather than assuming that a fluent answer is correct.
syllabus.project: RAG quality report with a small evaluation dataset and cited outputs.

syllabus.title: Weeks 13–15 | AI Agents and Tool Calling
syllabus.body: Build a tool-using assistant that selects actions within clear rules. Learn why reliable agents need permission boundaries, timeouts and explicit failure paths.

syllabus.title: Weeks 16–18 | LangGraph and Human Approval
topics: State graphs, nodes, edges and routing
syllabus.body: Use LangGraph to represent multi-step decisions as a stateful workflow. Make sensitive actions pause for approval and resume safely after review.

syllabus.body: Compare single-agent and multi-agent architectures. Build a small coordinated workflow only where separate specialist responsibilities actually improve clarity.

topics: Tracing, cost tracking and failure analysis
syllabus.body: Test the application as software, not only as a chat demo. Include adversarial inputs, retrieval failures, latency checks and safe fallback behavior.

overview:
Six-Month Agentic AI Training in Mohali

The Agentic AI course in Mohali develops practical skill in Python, LLM APIs, LangChain, RAG and LangGraph. A six-month roadmap creates room for foundational coding, source-grounded applications, bounded tool use, testing and a final capstone. Learners gain a clearer understanding of how modern AI software is designed, rather than collecting disconnected prompt examples.

From Prompt Engineering to Structured LLM Applications

A reliable language-model application needs more than a clever prompt. Learners explore prompt templates, token constraints, model limitations, typed JSON outputs and API error handling. The practical objective is to produce predictable data for the next component in a workflow and to understand how an application should respond when the model output is incomplete or inconsistent.

Practical Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Vector Search

RAG combines document processing, embeddings, retrieval and answer generation so a system can work with a specified knowledge base. The curriculum examines chunking, metadata and source provenance as well as vector search tools such as Chroma, FAISS and Qdrant. Learners practise evaluating whether retrieved passages support the resulting answer.

Build Controlled AI Agents with LangChain

LangChain provides components for integrating models, retrievers and tools. Students can develop agents that call read-only APIs, interpret structured results and draft useful next steps. They also examine tool permission boundaries and stop conditions. The intended skill is knowing how to build and debug a tool-using workflow safely, not assuming that an agent should control every action.

LangGraph, State and Human Approval

LangGraph supports stateful orchestration, checkpoints and human-in-the-loop patterns. Learners construct workflows with branches and resume points, then demonstrate that a sensitive request waits for explicit approval. This introduces important production concepts: traceability, recoverability and responsibility for decisions delegated to software.

AI Project Portfolio and Technical Evaluation

Projects include a knowledge assistant, support triage workflow, retrieval benchmark, research checker and final integrated capstone. Each planned assignment has a defined deliverable, such as tested code, a demonstration, a short evaluation report or deployment documentation. The finished portfolio should explain what the application does, where it can fail and why the chosen design is appropriate.

Deployment and Career Skills

Students learn how FastAPI, Docker, GitHub and automated tests support AI application delivery. These skills can complement preparation for junior AI engineering and LLM integration positions. The exact curriculum, class hours and available career assistance should be confirmed with techcadd Mohali; training does not guarantee employment.
